pr_title: net: sockets: prevent zephyr fatal in dns resolving callback
pr_body:
if dns request was attempted
in the absence of network connection,
and then network is present again after more than
CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DNS_TIMEOUT + 100,
ZEPHYR FATAL happens

Fixes #39242

Signed-off-by: Andrey Dodonov <andrey.dodonov@endress.com>

issue_context.title: net: sockets: Zephyr Fatal in dns_resolve_cb if dns request was attempted in offline state
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

In case if dns resolving was attempted in offline state,
going back online triggers Zephyr Fatal.

Source of the crash:
subsys\net\lib\sockets\getaddrinfo.c

The reason is that `dns_resolve_cb` tries to give semaphore which doesn't exist anymore.
Error lifecycle:
- `z_impl_z_zsock_getaddrinfo_internal ` creates semaphore as part of `struct getaddrinfo_state ai_state;`
- it waits for the semaphore: `k_sem_take(&ai_state.sem, K_MSEC(CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DNS_TIMEOUT + 100));`
- if semaphore was not given, it returns: `if (ret == -EAGAIN) {return DNS_EAI_AGAIN;}`, thus deallocating the semaphore
- we are back online (e.g. wifi network is back up, cable plugged, etc.), and thread rx_q eventually calls `dns_resolve_cb`
- `dns_resolve_cb` tries to give the semaphore:  `k_sem_give(&state->sem);`. But it doesn't exist anymore. ZEPHYR FATAL.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Any platform with network connectivity 
2. Call zsock_getaddrinfo when the internet is not present.
3. After  K_MSEC(CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DNS_TIMEOUT + 100) get back online (platform-depedent)
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
No crash occurs.

**Impact**
It is showstopper, because there can be many reasons for network disconnects and business logic doesn't have to check low-level connection state (loose coupling).

Imagine if your PC goes offline (e.g. wi-fi network down), meanwhie you attempt to make a `git push`. Or send an e-mail.
Then you go back online and enjoy BSOD.

**Logs and console output**
```
[00:00:14.225,128] <err> os: ***** HARD FAULT *****
[00:00:14.231,018] <err> os:   Fault escalation (see below)
[00:00:14.237,609] <err> os: ***** BUS FAULT *****
[00:00:14.243,408] <err> os:   Precise data bus error
[00:00:14.249,481] <err> os:   BFAR Address: 0x6174626f
[00:00:14.255,798] <err> os: r0/a1:  0x64656e69  r1/a2:  0x0006a504  r2/a3:  0x6174626f
[00:00:14.265,045] <err> os: r3/a4:  0x20746f4e r12/ip:  0x000000fe r14/lr:  0x000659d3 
[00:00:14.274,261] <err> os:  xpsr:  0x21000000
[00:00:14.279,846] <err> os: Faulting instruction address (r15/pc): 0x000657a6
[00:00:14.288,208] <err> os: >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 0: CPU exception on CPU 0
[00:00:14.296,478] <err> os: Current thread: 0x20016018 (rx_q[0])
[00:00:14.308,715] <err> os: Halting system
```
**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Interestingly enough, faulting instruction resolves to zephyr/include/sys/dlist.h:513 (with addr2line tool), and 
r14/lr:  0x000659d3  to kernel/include/ksched.h:167
Probably because scheduler crashes on an attempt to access some random address as semaphore.

**Additional context**
Minimalistic and most robust fix would be to make structure with semaphore static, e.g.
in `z_impl_z_zsock_getaddrinfo_internal`:
`static struct getaddrinfo_state ai_state;`

review_comments:
`ai_state` should not be `static`.

The semaphore timeout is set to a higher value than the DNS timeout to prevent this issue, maybe the mechanism fails in this specific case and a DNS cancel is required.

Timing can be extremely platform dependent, so +100 seems like a workaround.
So why not static to cover all the edge cases?

Also what I observed is that dns callback was still called arbitrary time after dns request, once we went back online.
Which is probably a separate issue.
Changing the variable to `static` would make it impossible to call `getaddrinfo` from multiple threads.

I see. I agree that some other solution is needed in this case.
I'll make changes to the PR.

Seems like dns_resolve_cb being called is the issue here.
Still, +100 is also not reliable.

May be the easiest fix (or workaround?) would be checking for the pointer validity in dns_resolve_cb.
`dns_resolve_cb` itself can't validate the stored pointer, it's up to the API caller to cancel the request if the callback goes out of scope.

Wouldn't it be enough to call `dns_cancel_addr_info()` in case of timeout, to make sure the query is actually cancelled in case some weird scheduling delay takes place? The callback shall be no longer executed after the query was cancelled and it should make no harm to cancel twice from what I've checked. `exec_query()` should keep the `dns_id` in such case though.

> However, it seems like a workaround, because request has to be cancelled by that time in the first place.

In normal condition, yes, it should've been canceled. The `dns_write()` function sets a [delayed work](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c#L927) for the timeout handling, which should [cancel the request](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c#L1054). `getaddrinfo` gives a 100 ms window for the delayed work to be executed and request canceled.

But in your case, I assume the delayed work was not executed for whatever reason within this period (perhaps one of the threads in your application is busy-looping?) and the thread that executes `getaddrinfo`  takes precedence, effectively releasing the semaphore before the query is cancelled. And if [cb_recv()](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c#L769) kicks in after that, we have a crash.

Therefore I don't think that cancelling the query from `getaddrinfo` context should be considered as a workaround, but rather a reasonable precaution for some unexpected system work queue delays.
